summary.text: A functional group is a substituent or moiety in a molecule that causes the molecule's characteristic chemical reactions.
The same functional group undergoes the same or similar reactions regardless of the rest of the molecule, which lets chemists predict reactions and design syntheses.
Functional groups also shape solubility: under the rule 'like dissolves like', sugar dissolves in water because both share the hydroxyl group.

facts.label: Ligands
facts.value: Groups binding a central atom in a coordination complex

facts.label: Alpha carbon
facts.value: First carbon after the one bearing the group

items.prompt: Sugar stirs into a glass of water and disappears. Which idea about molecules best explains it?

options.label: Sugar is a solid, so it can only break apart where water is a gas
Water molecules are smaller, so sugar fits between them without bonding
Both carry the same kind of group, and those groups attract each other strongly
Both are nonpolar molecules, and nonpolar molecules mix with everything

items.explain: 'Like dissolves like': sugar and water share the hydroxyl group, and hydroxyls interact strongly with each other.

items.prompt: A chemist meets a huge, unfamiliar molecule that contains a group she knows well. What should she expect from that group?

options.label: Similar reactions to those it undergoes elsewhere, though nearby groups can shift it
Exactly the same reactions, with nothing nearby able to change them
Reactions she cannot predict until the whole molecule is studied
No reactions at all, because the rest of the molecule is too large

items.explain: A functional group reacts the same or similarly regardless of the rest of the molecule, but nearby functional groups can modify its reactivity.

items.prompt: A chemist calls the left half of a molecule a moiety. How does a moiety relate to a functional group?

options.label: A moiety is always exactly one functional group
A moiety can be one functional group or a larger unit made of several
A moiety is the part of a molecule that has no functional groups
A moiety is any charged group, like a carboxylate salt's group

items.explain: A moiety is an entire 'half' of a molecule, which can be a single functional group or a larger unit of several.

items.prompt: A molecule that barely mixes with water gains a group more electronegative than the atoms it attaches to. What happens to the molecule?

options.label: It stays unable to mix with water
It turns charged and so splits into two separate molecules
It becomes a ligand and so binds to a central atom
It becomes polar and so soluble in some aqueous environment

items.explain: Groups more electronegative than their attachment atoms become polar, which makes otherwise nonpolar molecules polar and soluble in some aqueous environment.

items.prompt: Sulfur sits just below oxygen on the periodic table, yet sulfur compounds behave in their own way. What ability explains this?

options.label: Sulfur is lighter than oxygen, so it moves more freely
Sulfur can form more bonds than oxygen
Sulfur cannot bond to carbon at all, unlike oxygen
Sulfur carries a partially filled octet, so it acts as an acid

items.explain: Compounds containing sulfur show unique chemistry due to sulfur's ability to form more bonds than oxygen, its lighter analogue.

items.prompt: A chemist compares an iodoalkane with a fluoroalkane. Which has the more stable carbon–halogen bond?

options.label: The iodoalkane
Neither; haloalkane bonds are all equally stable
The fluoroalkane
Neither; haloalkanes have no carbon–halogen bond

items.explain: The carbon–halogen bond can be relatively weak, as in an iodoalkane, or quite stable, as in a fluoroalkane.
